This is a letter. Headed Paris, December 16, 1956. Dear Mr. LaRocca, The very long trip I have done through the world is at its end. I am just arrived from Melbourne this morning with a great regret not to have been in New Orleans for meeting you. But fate is blind and can offer me a very next opportunity to go to the States for another film. I suppose you have well received my letter dated November the 11th that I have sent you from Calcutta. ctx.x: Yeah, but how long, I mean when was the last time though?

In 1938 I reorganized the band. When this music was being taken away from New Orleans, they were calling Chicago Swing. Benny Goodman was in the center then. And what he played, if you look at it, the St. Louis Blues is a copy for my cornet part and also Larry Shields' clarinet part. He had mixed to listen to the records of the original Lixieland Jazz Band when he was only eight years old. And I played, when I first started playing in a group, it would have been about 1904.
